deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages. pi is the (profinite, or discrete) fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,infty}. It has inertia subgroups L_0, L_1, L_infty, generated by l_0, l_1, l_infty with l_0 l_1 l_infty = 1.

- Gamma ~ S_3 x Z/2 is the group of symmetries of the three-punctured line: S_3 permutes the cusps, and tau is complex conjugation.
- E is the extension of Gamma by pi. In the discrete case it is the orbifold fundamental group of the modular-type quotient, i.e. PGL_2(Z) with kernel Gamma(2)/{±1}.
- SE (and its profinite version) consists of the tuples (p, sigma, g_0, g_1, g_infty), with p in Z^*, sigma in S_3 and g_i in pi. Such a tuple is the automorphism sending l_i to the conjugate int(g_i)(l_{sigma(i)}^p), subject to the product relation (12)/(13).
- The previous page identified the rigid lifts Gamma~_p (all g_i = 1).

This page has three parts.

(1) Which subgroups of Gamma lift. The 2-Sylow subgroups <sigma_i, tau> ~ Z/2 x Z/2 of Gamma do not lift. Grothendieck's reason is that the local extension of Gamma_0^+ (the orientation-preserving stabilizer of the cusp 0, of order 2) by the inertia Z_0 is non-split. Concretely, the cusp stabilizer in PSL_2 is generated by T, with T^2 in Gamma(2), so the extension is Z --x2--> Z --> Z/2. Hence sigma_0 has no order-2 lift that normalizes L_0. He declines to write presentations of SGamma and SE.

(2) Conjugation formulas, using the lifts rho~ (of the 3-cycle rho) and sigma~_0:
- (15): int(rho~) sends (p, sigma, g_0, g_1, g_infty) to (p, rho sigma rho^-1, rho(g_infty), rho(g_0), rho(g_1)).
- (16): int(sigma~_0) sends it to (p, sigma_0 sigma sigma_0^-1, sigma_0(g_0), sigma_0(g_infty), sigma_0(g_1)).

(3) Centralizers.
- u~ commutes with rho~ exactly when sigma lies in A_3 and (17) holds: g_1 = rho(g_0), g_infty = rho(g_1), g_0 = rho(g_infty). So everything is determined by g_0, with g_infty = rho^2(g_0) = rho^-1(g_0).
- The next page substitutes this into the product relation, giving (18): int(rho^2 g_0)(l^p) . int(rho g_0)(l^p) . int(g_0)(l^p) = 1. This is a cyclic 3-term relation in the single unknown g_0, and is essentially Drinfeld's hexagon relation (II) for GT.
- Commutation with sigma~_0 gives g_0 = sigma_0(g_0) and g_infty = sigma_0(g_1). This is the analogue of the 2-cycle relation (I).

Overall purpose: to cut the big group SE^ down to the elements commuting with the S_3 (or Gamma) symmetry. This is an early, pre-Drinfeld derivation of the defining relations of the genus-0, four-point (M_{0,4}) level of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group.
errors: The claim that the Klein four subgroups <sigma_i, tau> 'do not lift' is too strong as stated, at least for the discrete E = PGL_2(Z). The stabilizer of the elliptic point i (the right-angle vertex of the (2,3,infty) reflection triangle) is a Klein four group. It maps isomorphically onto <s, tau> in Gamma = PGL_2(Z)/(Gamma(2)/±1) ~ S_3 x Z/2. So these 2-Sylows do lift, as stabilizers of the order-2 elliptic point. What Grothendieck's argument actually proves is weaker: sigma_i admits no order-2 lift normalizing the inertia L_i at its fixed cusp (non-split cusp extension). The intended statement is presumably 'no lift compatible with the cusp/inertia rigidification'.
Minor: 'les extensions locales ... n'est pas scindée' (plural/singular slip). (17) contains a redundant third equation, which the next page notes.

ideas.what: Non-splitting of the local extension of the cusp stabilizer Gamma_0^+ by inertia Z_0; obstruction to lifting the 2-Sylows of the symmetry group compatibly with inertia
ideas.modern_name: Cusp stabilizers in PSL_2(Z) vs Gamma(2); non-split extension Z->Z->Z/2; orbifold pi_1 of M_{0,4}/S_3
ideas.where_published: possibly echoed in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated)

ideas.what: Explicit formulas for conjugation by lifts of rho and sigma_0 on the tuples (p, sigma, g_0, g_1, g_infty) describing automorphisms of pi^ that normalize the inertia classes
ideas.modern_name: S_3-action on 'GT-type' tuples (lambda, f) / action of the Klein-four symmetries on M_{0,4}
ideas.where_published: related material in La Longue Marche (1981); idea sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Centralizer of the order-3 symmetry: g_1 = rho(g_0), g_infty = rho^2(g_0), leading to the cyclic relation (18) in a single g_0; centralizer of sigma_0 gives g_0 = sigma_0(g_0)
ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld's hexagon (relation II) and 2-cycle (relation I) for GT^; GT_0 as the automorphisms of pi_1(M_{0,4}) commuting with the S_3 action
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme states that Gal(Q-bar/Q) should be describable via the genus-0 Teichmüller tower at levels n <= 5. The explicit relations are not published there to my knowledge.

missed.claim: In spring 1981 Grothendieck explicitly derived the S_3-equivariance conditions on the 'rectifiers' (g_0, g_1, g_infty). These reduce the data to one element g_0 with g_1 = rho(g_0), g_infty = rho^2(g_0), plus a cyclic product relation in the inertia powers l^p. This is essentially Drinfeld's relation (II) for GT^, derived nine years earlier. The sigma_0-centralizer condition parallels relation (I).
missed.quote: Pour que ũ commute à ρ, il f. et s. que σ commute à ρ i.e. σ∈{1,ρ,ρ²}, et qu'on ait (17) g_1=ρ(g_0), g_∞=ρ(g_1), g_0=ρ(g_∞)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents precisely how close Grothendieck came to the definition of GT (minus the pentagon). It is of historical interest for crediting the S_3-equivariant characterization of GT_0. It is not new mathematics today.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows Grothendieck, in 1981, mechanically deriving the 3-cycle (hexagon-type) relation of GT^ from commutation with the order-3 symmetry. Historians know he anticipated GT in a general way (Esquisse, Longue Marche), but this explicit derivation in this draft is a notable unpublished detail. The mathematics itself has been fully superseded by Drinfeld, Ihara and Lochak–Schneps.
